BM1-IE402-001 · Course-CLO

verified-syllabus · IE-402 · Systems Engineering · academic-semantic

Source

Course: IE-402 - Systems Engineering
Program: BSIE
Description: This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,
design, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students
learn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and
operational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and
performance evaluation. 
Students will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They
will explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as
manufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that
maximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. 
Beyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the
development of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also
instills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped
with the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering.

Target

Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of engineering and management principles by effectively leading and collaborating within teams, managing projects, and engaging in multidisciplinary environments.

BM1-IE402-011 · Course-CLO

verified-syllabus · IE-402 · Systems Engineering · academic-semantic

Source

Course: IE-402 - Systems Engineering
Program: BSIE
Description: This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,
design, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students
learn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and
operational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and
performance evaluation. 
Students will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They
will explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as
manufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that
maximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. 
Beyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the
development of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also
instills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped
with the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering.

Target

Develop the ability to identify and solve systems engineering challenges, making decisions that improve performance, enhance efficiency, and support sustainable practices across diverse industries.

BM1-IE402-019 · Course-CLO

verified-syllabus · IE-402 · Systems Engineering · academic-semantic

Source

Course: IE-402 - Systems Engineering
Program: BSIE
Description: This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,
design, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students
learn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and
operational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and
performance evaluation. 
Students will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They
will explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as
manufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that
maximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. 
Beyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the
development of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also
instills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped
with the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering.

Target

Demonstrate the Filipino- Catholic Augustinian Spirituality through value webbing.

{

  },
  "description": [
    {
      "id": "ie402_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,\ndesign, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students\nlearn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and\noperational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and\nperformance evaluation. \nStudents will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They\nwill explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as\nmanufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that\nmaximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. \nBeyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the\ndevelopment of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also\ninstills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped\nwith the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering."
    }
  ],

BM1-IE402-030 · ILO-CLO

verified-syllabus · IE-402 · Systems Engineering · academic-semantic

Source

Apply critical and creative thinking skills to analyze, design, and optimize complex systems, integrating various components such as people, materials, technology, and information.

Target

ILO2: Develop basic system designs that incorporate requirements from multiple disciplines, including human factors, technology, and organizational needs. [CLO 1], [CLO 2]

{
  "meta": {

    "schoolYear": "2025-2026",
    "curriculumYear": "",

    "prereq": "4th Year Standing",
    "lecture": "",
    "lab": ""
  },
  "description": [
    {
      "id": "ie402_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,\ndesign, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students\nlearn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and\noperational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and\nperformance evaluation. \nStudents will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They\nwill explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as\nmanufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that\nmaximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. \nBeyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the\ndevelopment of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also\ninstills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped\nwith the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering."
    }
  ],

  "description": [
    {
      "id": "ie402_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,\ndesign, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students\nlearn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and\noperational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and\nperformance evaluation. \nStudents will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They\nwill explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as\nmanufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that\nmaximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. \nBeyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the\ndevelopment of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also\ninstills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped\nwith the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering."
    }

    {
      "id": "ie402_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,\ndesign, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students\nlearn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and\noperational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and\nperformance evaluation. \nStudents will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They\nwill explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as\nmanufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that\nmaximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. \nBeyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the\ndevelopment of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also\ninstills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped\nwith the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering."

      "id": "ie402_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,\ndesign, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students\nlearn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and\noperational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and\nperformance evaluation. \nStudents will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They\nwill explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as\nmanufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that\nmaximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. \nBeyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the\ndevelopment of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also\ninstills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped\nwith the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering."

BM1-IE402-040 · ILO-CLO

verified-syllabus · IE-402 · Systems Engineering · academic-semantic

Source

Develop the ability to identify and solve systems engineering challenges, making decisions that improve performance, enhance efficiency, and support sustainable practices across diverse industries.

Target

ILO5: Recognize key outputs of the systems engineering process, such as documentation, specifications, and test reports, and evaluate their role in supporting successful project outcomes. [CLO2][CLO3]

  "description": [
    {
      "id": "ie402_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,\ndesign, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students\nlearn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and\noperational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and\nperformance evaluation. \nStudents will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They\nwill explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as\nmanufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that\nmaximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. \nBeyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the\ndevelopment of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also\ninstills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped\nwith the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering."
    }

  "description": [
    {
      "id": "ie402_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,\ndesign, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students\nlearn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and\noperational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and\nperformance evaluation. \nStudents will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They\nwill explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as\nmanufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that\nmaximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. \nBeyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the\ndevelopment of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also\ninstills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped\nwith the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering."

They\nwill explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as\nmanufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that\nmaximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. \nBeyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the\ndevelopment of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also\ninstills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped\nwith the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering."

    {
      "id": "ie402_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,\ndesign, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students\nlearn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and\noperational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and\nperformance evaluation. \nStudents will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They\nwill explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as\nmanufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that\nmaximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. \nBeyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the\ndevelopment of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also\ninstills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped\nwith the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering."

      "id": "ie402_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,\ndesign, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students\nlearn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and\noperational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and\nperformance evaluation. \nStudents will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They\nwill explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as\nmanufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that\nmaximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. \nBeyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the\ndevelopment of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also\ninstills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped\nwith the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering."

    {
      "id": "ie402_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,\ndesign, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students\nlearn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and\noperational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and\nperformance evaluation. \nStudents will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They\nwill explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as\nmanufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that\nmaximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. \nBeyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the\ndevelopment of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also\ninstills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped\nwith the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering."

      "id": "ie402_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,\ndesign, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students\nlearn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and\noperational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and\nperformance evaluation. \nStudents will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They\nwill explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as\nmanufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that\nmaximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. \nBeyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the\ndevelopment of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also\ninstills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped\nwith the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering."
    }

BM1-IE402-055 · ILO-activity

verified-syllabus · IE-402 · Systems Engineering · academic-semantic

Source

ILO9: Formulate a comprehensive systems engineering plan that outlines objectives, resources, timelines, and milestones to guide system development from inception through completion. [CLO 3] [CLO4]

Target

Workshop on Systems
Engineering Planning
Conduct a hands-on
workshop where students
outline a systems
engineering plan for a
hypothetical project. They
should include project
objectives, resource
allocation, timeline
planning, and key
milestones.
Product Improvement
Strategy Brainstorming
Session
In groups, students
brainstorm and propose
strategies for iterative
product improvement in a
given scenario, focusing
on design, functionality,
and customer feedback
loops.

  "description": [
    {
      "id": "ie402_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,\ndesign, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students\nlearn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and\noperational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and\nperformance evaluation. \nStudents will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They\nwill explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as\nmanufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that\nmaximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. \nBeyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the\ndevelopment of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also\ninstills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped\nwith the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering."

Target

Workshop on Systems
Engineering Planning
Conduct a hands-on
workshop where students
outline a systems
engineering plan for a
hypothetical project. They
should include project
objectives, resource
allocation, timeline
planning, and key
milestones.
Product Improvement
Strategy Brainstorming
Session
In groups, students
brainstorm and propose
strategies for iterative
product improvement in a
given scenario, focusing
on design, functionality,
and customer feedback
loops.

BM1-IE402-060 · ILO-CLO

verified-syllabus · IE-402 · Systems Engineering · academic-semantic

Source

Develop the ability to identify and solve systems engineering challenges, making decisions that improve performance, enhance efficiency, and support sustainable practices across diverse industries.

Target

ILO11: Analyze and evaluate multiple design alternatives through trade space exploration, applying criteria to select the optimal concept based on performance, feasibility, and stakeholder needs. [CLO 3] [CLO4]

  "description": [
    {
      "id": "ie402_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,\ndesign, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students\nlearn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and\noperational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and\nperformance evaluation. \nStudents will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They\nwill explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as\nmanufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that\nmaximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. \nBeyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the\ndevelopment of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also\ninstills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped\nwith the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering."
    }

BM1-IE402-062 · ILO-activity

verified-syllabus · IE-402 · Systems Engineering · academic-semantic

Source

ILO11: Analyze and evaluate multiple design alternatives through trade space exploration, applying criteria to select the optimal concept based on performance, feasibility, and stakeholder needs. [CLO 3] [CLO4]

Target

Case Study Discussion:
Systems Engineering
as a Human Activity
Provide a case study that
highlights the role of
human factors in systems
engineering, including
team dynamics,
stakeholder involvement,
and ethical
considerations. Facilitate
a class discussion on the
human-centered aspects
and their impact on
project outcomes.
Design and Conduct
Experiments Activity
Assign students a mini-
project to design and
conduct an experiment to
validate a system
component or process.
They should identify the
objective, develop a
methodology, collect
data, and analyze results
to inform design
improvements.
Robust Design
Brainstorming Session
(Robust Design I)
In small groups, students
brainstorm how to apply
basic robust design
principles to make a
system more stable
under varying conditions.
They discuss factors that
influence system stability
and propose design
adjustments to minimize
variability.
Advanced Robust
Design Project (Robust
Design II)
Activity: For a more
complex project, students
apply advanced robust
design techniques to a
hypothetical or real-world
system. They identify and
control multiple variables
to minimize performance
variation across diverse
scenarios.

  "description": [
    {
      "id": "ie402_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,\ndesign, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students\nlearn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and\noperational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and\nperformance evaluation. \nStudents will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They\nwill explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as\nmanufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that\nmaximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. \nBeyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the\ndevelopment of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also\ninstills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped\nwith the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering."
    }

  "description": [
    {
      "id": "ie402_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,\ndesign, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students\nlearn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and\noperational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and\nperformance evaluation. \nStudents will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They\nwill explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as\nmanufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that\nmaximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. \nBeyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the\ndevelopment of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also\ninstills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped\nwith the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering."
    }
  ],

BM1-IE402-065 · ILO-activity

verified-syllabus · IE-402 · Systems Engineering · academic-semantic

Source

ILO 12: Develop and execute experiments to validate design assumptions, analyze system behaviors, and refine solutions, demonstrating an understanding of experimental design and data collection principles. [CLO 3] [CLO4]

Target

Case Study Discussion:
Systems Engineering
as a Human Activity
Provide a case study that
highlights the role of
human factors in systems
engineering, including
team dynamics,
stakeholder involvement,
and ethical
considerations. Facilitate
a class discussion on the
human-centered aspects
and their impact on
project outcomes.
Design and Conduct
Experiments Activity
Assign students a mini-
project to design and
conduct an experiment to
validate a system
component or process.
They should identify the
objective, develop a
methodology, collect
data, and analyze results
to inform design
improvements.
Robust Design
Brainstorming Session
(Robust Design I)
In small groups, students
brainstorm how to apply
basic robust design
principles to make a
system more stable
under varying conditions.
They discuss factors that
influence system stability
and propose design
adjustments to minimize
variability.
Advanced Robust
Design Project (Robust
Design II)
Activity: For a more
complex project, students
apply advanced robust
design techniques to a
hypothetical or real-world
system. They identify and
control multiple variables
to minimize performance
variation across diverse
scenarios.

BM1-IE402-066 · ILO-CLO

verified-syllabus · IE-402 · Systems Engineering · academic-semantic

Source

Develop the ability to identify and solve systems engineering challenges, making decisions that improve performance, enhance efficiency, and support sustainable practices across diverse industries.

Target

ILO 13: Identify critical factors in system design that influence performance consistency, and apply robust design techniques to improve reliability under varying conditions (Robust Design I). [CLO 3] [CLO4]

  "description": [
    {
      "id": "ie402_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,\ndesign, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students\nlearn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and\noperational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and\nperformance evaluation. \nStudents will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They\nwill explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as\nmanufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that\nmaximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. \nBeyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the\ndevelopment of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also\ninstills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped\nwith the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering."
    }

BM1-IE402-068 · ILO-activity

verified-syllabus · IE-402 · Systems Engineering · academic-semantic

Source

ILO 13: Identify critical factors in system design that influence performance consistency, and apply robust design techniques to improve reliability under varying conditions (Robust Design I). [CLO 3] [CLO4]

Target

Case Study Discussion:
Systems Engineering
as a Human Activity
Provide a case study that
highlights the role of
human factors in systems
engineering, including
team dynamics,
stakeholder involvement,
and ethical
considerations. Facilitate
a class discussion on the
human-centered aspects
and their impact on
project outcomes.
Design and Conduct
Experiments Activity
Assign students a mini-
project to design and
conduct an experiment to
validate a system
component or process.
They should identify the
objective, develop a
methodology, collect
data, and analyze results
to inform design
improvements.
Robust Design
Brainstorming Session
(Robust Design I)
In small groups, students
brainstorm how to apply
basic robust design
principles to make a
system more stable
under varying conditions.
They discuss factors that
influence system stability
and propose design
adjustments to minimize
variability.
Advanced Robust
Design Project (Robust
Design II)
Activity: For a more
complex project, students
apply advanced robust
design techniques to a
hypothetical or real-world
system. They identify and
control multiple variables
to minimize performance
variation across diverse
scenarios.

  "description": [
    {
      "id": "ie402_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,\ndesign, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students\nlearn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and\noperational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and\nperformance evaluation. \nStudents will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They\nwill explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as\nmanufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that\nmaximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. \nBeyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the\ndevelopment of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also\ninstills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped\nwith the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering."

  "description": [
    {
      "id": "ie402_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,\ndesign, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students\nlearn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and\noperational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and\nperformance evaluation. \nStudents will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They\nwill explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as\nmanufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that\nmaximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. \nBeyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the\ndevelopment of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also\ninstills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped\nwith the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering."
    }
  ],

Design and Conduct
Experiments Activity
Assign students a mini-
project to design and
conduct an experiment to
validate a system
component or process.
They should identify the
objective, develop a
methodology, collect
data, and analyze results
to inform design
improvements.
Robust Design
Brainstorming Session
(Robust Design I)
In small groups, students
brainstorm how to apply
basic robust design
principles to make a
system more stable
under varying conditions.
They discuss factors that
influence system stability
and propose design
adjustments to minimize
variability.
Advanced Robust
Design Project (Robust
Design II)
Activity: For a more
complex project, students
apply advanced robust
design techniques to a
hypothetical or real-world
system. They identify and
control multiple variables
to minimize performance
variation across diverse
scenarios.

  "description": [
    {
      "id": "ie402_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,\ndesign, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students\nlearn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and\noperational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and\nperformance evaluation. \nStudents will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They\nwill explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as\nmanufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that\nmaximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. \nBeyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the\ndevelopment of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also\ninstills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped\nwith the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering."
    }
  ],

{

  },
  "description": [
    {
      "id": "ie402_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,\ndesign, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students\nlearn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and\noperational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and\nperformance evaluation. \nStudents will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They\nwill explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as\nmanufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that\nmaximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. \nBeyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the\ndevelopment of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also\ninstills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped\nwith the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering."

      "id": "ie402_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,\ndesign, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students\nlearn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and\noperational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and\nperformance evaluation. \nStudents will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They\nwill explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as\nmanufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that\nmaximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. \nBeyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the\ndevelopment of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also\ninstills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service.       "id": "ie402_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,\ndesign, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students\nlearn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and\noperational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and\nperformance evaluation. \nStudents will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They\nwill explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as\nmanufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that\nmaximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. \nBeyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the\ndevelopment of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also\ninstills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped\nwith the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering."

      "id": "ie402_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,\ndesign, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students\nlearn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and\noperational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and\nperformance evaluation. \nStudents will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They\nwill explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as\nmanufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that\nmaximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. \nBeyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the\ndevelopment of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also\ninstills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service.   "description": [
    {
      "id": "ie402_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,\ndesign, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students\nlearn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and\noperational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and\nperformance evaluation. \nStudents will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They\nwill explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as\nmanufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that\nmaximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. \nBeyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the\ndevelopment of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also\ninstills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped\nwith the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering."
    }

Course: IE-402 - Systems Engineering
Program: BSIE
Week under review: 12-14 of 18
Previous week - Week 10-11: Systems Analysis and Control • Work Breakdown Structure • Configuration Management • Technical Reviews and Audits • Trade Studies • Modeling and Simulation • Me
Next week - Week 15-17: Application • Systems Engineering As Human Activity • Trade Space Exploration Concept Selection • Experiments • Robust Design I • Robust Design II

and Managing

    {
      "id": "ie402_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,\ndesign, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students\nlearn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and\noperational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and\nperformance evaluation. \nStudents will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They\nwill explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as\nmanufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that\nmaximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. \nBeyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the\ndevelopment of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also\ninstills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped\nwith the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering."
    }

  "description": [
    {
      "id": "ie402_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,\ndesign, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students\nlearn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and\noperational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and\nperformance evaluation. \nStudents will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They\nwill explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as\nmanufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that\nmaximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. \nBeyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the\ndevelopment of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also\ninstills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped\nwith the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering."
    }

  "description": [
    {
      "id": "ie402_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,\ndesign, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students\nlearn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and\noperational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and\nperformance evaluation. \nStudents will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They\nwill explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as\nmanufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that\nmaximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. \nBeyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the\ndevelopment of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also\ninstills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped\nwith the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering."
    }

Target

This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,
design, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students
learn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and
operational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and
performance evaluation. 
Students will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They
will explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as
manufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that
maximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. 
Beyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the
development of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also
instills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped
with the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering.

  "description": [
    {
      "id": "ie402_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,\ndesign, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students\nlearn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and\noperational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and\nperformance evaluation. \nStudents will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They\nwill explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as\nmanufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that\nmaximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. \nBeyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the\ndevelopment of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also\ninstills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped\nwith the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering."
    }

BM1-IE402-095 · CLO-classification

verified-syllabus · IE-402 · Systems Engineering · academic-semantic

Source

Systems Engineering
BSIE
This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,
design, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students
learn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and
operational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and
performance evaluation. 
Students will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They
will explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as
manufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that
maximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. 
Beyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the
development of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also
instills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped
with the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Assigned classification: Introductory

Target

Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of engineering and management principles by effectively leading and collaborating within teams, managing projects, and engaging in multidisciplinary environments.

BM1-IE402-098 · CLO-classification

verified-syllabus · IE-402 · Systems Engineering · academic-semantic

Source

Systems Engineering
BSIE
This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,
design, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students
learn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and
operational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and
performance evaluation. 
Students will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They
will explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as
manufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that
maximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. 
Beyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the
development of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also
instills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped
with the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Assigned classification: Introductory

Target

Demonstrate the Filipino- Catholic Augustinian Spirituality through value webbing.

reference-data/IE402-SYSTEM-ENGINEERINGS.pdf; SHA256 44ca6d48c77d0b04055cf330717b9381b64d3b7fb8674be727aa2eb4a1807569; pages 1, 2, 4, 5
Original course context and source excerpts
{
  "meta": {
    "program": "BSIE",
    "code": "IE-402",
    "title": "Systems Engineering",
    "schoolYear": "2025-2026",
    "curriculumYear": "",
    "yearLevel": "",
    "prereq": "4th Year Standing",
    "lecture": "",
    "lab": ""
  },
  "description": [
    {
      "id": "ie402_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,\ndesign, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students\nlearn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and\noperational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and\nperformance evaluation. \nStudents will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They\nwill explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as\nmanufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that\nmaximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. \nBeyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the\ndevelopment of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also\ninstills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped\nwith the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering."
    }
  ],

  "description": [
    {
      "id": "ie402_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,\ndesign, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students\nlearn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and\noperational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and\nperformance evaluation. \nStudents will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They\nwill explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as\nmanufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that\nmaximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. \nBeyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the\ndevelopment of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also\ninstills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped\nwith the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering."
    }

Analysis Report

scenario where they

and Allocation
Diagram

system, explaining
how the design
integrates functional
requirements and
meets project goals.

    {
      "id": "ie402_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,\ndesign, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students\nlearn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and\noperational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and\nperformance evaluation. \nStudents will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They\nwill explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as\nmanufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that\nmaximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. \nBeyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the\ndevelopment of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also\ninstills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped\nwith the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering."

BM1-IE402-108 · Content-activity

verified-syllabus · IE-402 · Systems Engineering · academic-semantic

Source

Week 10-11 course content: Systems Analysis
and Control
• Work
Breakdown
Structure
• Configuration
Management
• Technical
Reviews and
Audits
• Trade Studies
• Modeling and
Simulation
• Metrics
• Risk
Management

Target

Interactive Workshop
on Work Breakdown
Structure (WBS)
Creation
Activity: Conduct an
interactive workshop
where students create a
WBS for a hypothetical
project, breaking down
tasks and identifying
deliverables.
Case Study on
Configuration
Management
Activity: Present a case
study demonstrating
configuration
management principles
and practices in a real-
world project. Have
students discuss the role
of configuration
management in
maintaining system
consistency.
Risk Management
Analysis Activity
Activity: Present a
project scenario and ask
students to identify
potential risks, assess
their impact and
probability, and develop
mitigation strategies.

experimental design

approach.

strategies to address

      "t": "This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,\ndesign, and management of complex systems. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and\nperformance evaluation. \nStudents will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. Week 10-11 learning activities: Interactive Workshop
on Work Breakdown
Structure (WBS)
Creation
Activity: Conduct an
interactive workshop
where students create a
WBS for a hypothetical
project, breaking down
tasks and identifying
deliverables.
Case Study on
Configuration
Management
Activity: Present a case
study demonstrating
configuration
management principles
and practices in a real-
world project. Have
students discuss the role
of configuration
management in
maintaining system
consistency.
Risk Management
Analysis Activity
Activity: Present a
project scenario and ask
students to identify
potential risks, assess
their impact and
probability, and develop
mitigation strategies.

Peer Review of
Experimental Design
and Robustness
Plan
Ask students to peer
review each other’s
experimental design
proposals and
robustness plans,
providing constructive
feedback on
methodology and
approach.
Risk Assessment
and Mitigation in
Robust Design
Assign a task where
students assess
potential risks to
robustness in a
system design and
develop mitigation
strategies to address
these risks.

verified-syllabus · IE-402 · Systems Engineering · academic-semantic

Source

Week 12-14 course content: Planning, Organizing
and Managing
• Systems
Engineering
Planning
• Product
Improvement
Strategies
• Organizing and
Integrating
System
Development
• Contractual
Considerations
• Management
Considerations
and Summary

Target

Workshop on Systems
Engineering Planning
Conduct a hands-on
workshop where students
outline a systems
engineering plan for a
hypothetical project. They
should include project
objectives, resource
allocation, timeline
planning, and key
milestones.
Product Improvement
Strategy Brainstorming
Session
In groups, students
brainstorm and propose
strategies for iterative
product improvement in a
given scenario, focusing
on design, functionality,
and customer feedback
loops.

    {
      "id": "ie402_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,\ndesign, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students\nlearn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and\noperational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and\nperformance evaluation. \nStudents will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They\nwill explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as\nmanufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that\nmaximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. \nBeyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the\ndevelopment of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also\ninstills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped\nwith the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering."
    }

human factors in systems
engineering, including
team dynamics,
stakeholder involvement,
and ethical
considerations. Facilitate
a class discussion on the
human-centered aspects
and their impact on
project outcomes.
Design and Conduct
Experiments Activity
Assign students a mini-
project to design and
conduct an experiment to
validate a system
component or process.
They should identify the
objective, develop a
methodology, collect
data, and analyze results
to inform design
improvements.
Robust Design
Brainstorming Session
(Robust Design I)
In small groups, students
brainstorm how to apply
basic robust design
principles to make a
system more stable
under varying conditions.
They discuss factors that
influence system stability
and propose design
adjustments to minimize
variability.
Advanced Robust
Design Project (Robust
Design II)
Activity: For a more
complex project, students
apply advanced robust
design techniques to a
hypothetical or real-world
system. They identify and
control multiple variables
to minimize performance
variation across diverse
scenarios.

    {
      "id": "ie402_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,\ndesign, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students\nlearn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and\noperational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and\nperformance evaluation. \nStudents will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They\nwill explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as\nmanufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that\nmaximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. \nBeyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the\ndevelopment of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also\ninstills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped\nwith the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering."
    }

BM1-IE402-115 · Content-assessment

verified-syllabus · IE-402 · Systems Engineering · academic-semantic

Source

Week 15-17 course content: Application
• Systems
Engineering As
Human Activity
• Trade Space
Exploration
Concept
Selection
• Experiments
• Robust Design I
• Robust Design
II

Target

Robust Design I –
System Evaluation
and Improvement
Proposal
Task: Have students
apply basic robust
design techniques to
evaluate a system
and propose design
changes that would
make it more stable
under varying
conditions. They
should identify critical
factors that affect
performance and
suggest
improvements to
minimize variability.
Robust Design II –
Advanced Design
Analysis
Task: For a more
complex system,
students should apply
advanced robust
design methods to
assess and improve
the system’s
performance. They
will use tools such as
design of experiments
(DOE) to explore
multiple design
variables and their
interactions.
Robust Design
Report (I & II)
Task: Students will
submit a report for
each part of the
robust design
application, detailing
the steps taken to
assess and improve
system performance.
For Robust Design I,
they will focus on
basic principles, and
for Robust Design II,
they will apply
advanced techniques
to optimize the
system.

BM1-IE402-116 · Activity-assessment

verified-syllabus · IE-402 · Systems Engineering · academic-semantic

Source

Week 15-17 learning activities: Case Study Discussion:
Systems Engineering
as a Human Activity
Provide a case study that
highlights the role of
human factors in systems
engineering, including
team dynamics,
stakeholder involvement,
and ethical
considerations. Facilitate
a class discussion on the
human-centered aspects
and their impact on
project outcomes.
Design and Conduct
Experiments Activity
Assign students a mini-
project to design and
conduct an experiment to
validate a system
component or process.
They should identify the
objective, develop a
methodology, collect
data, and analyze results
to inform design
improvements.
Robust Design
Brainstorming Session
(Robust Design I)
In small groups, students
brainstorm how to apply
basic robust design
principles to make a
system more stable
under varying conditions.
They discuss factors that
influence system stability
and propose design
adjustments to minimize
variability.
Advanced Robust
Design Project (Robust
Design II)
Activity: For a more
complex project, students
apply advanced robust
design techniques to a
hypothetical or real-world
system. They identify and
control multiple variables
to minimize performance
variation across diverse
scenarios.

Target

Robust Design I –
System Evaluation
and Improvement
Proposal
Task: Have students
apply basic robust
design techniques to
evaluate a system
and propose design
changes that would
make it more stable
under varying
conditions. They
should identify critical
factors that affect
performance and
suggest
improvements to
minimize variability.
Robust Design II –
Advanced Design
Analysis
Task: For a more
complex system,
students should apply
advanced robust
design methods to
assess and improve
the system’s
performance. They
will use tools such as
design of experiments
(DOE) to explore
multiple design
variables and their
interactions.
Robust Design
Report (I & II)
Task: Students will
submit a report for
each part of the
robust design
application, detailing
the steps taken to
assess and improve
system performance.
For Robust Design I,
they will focus on
basic principles, and
for Robust Design II,
they will apply
advanced techniques
to optimize the
system.
